notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/transactionbubble.guide.tsx) and docs/evidence/transactionbubble.md at e7ed622 (“docs: publish 19 Component Fix fixes on jfs-components dbe0e02”, 28 October), the same files on main and docs-next. The guide's Sources note says it was checked on 28 October 2026 on the 27 October build of Biscuit's main, which is the installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02. The evidence's “dbe0e02 publish” section (#394, #346, verified 27 October, published 28 October) replaces the older sections where they differ; those (Checked, Contract, Tokens, Web render, Discrepancies) were checked on 25 October on v0.1.78-c8526ae. GitHub's compare of v0.1.78-c8526ae and v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (163 files) changes TransactionBubble.tsx, TransactionStatus.tsx and MoneyValue.tsx; installed copies match dbe0e02. MoneyValue changed only its accessibility (one named amount, #346), not its layout. TransactionStatus gained the mode-picked mark (#394), status copy from the mode, and disableTruncation. TransactionBubble at dbe0e02 also carries the #395 fixes the guide was not updated for, read from the installed source, not run: the default accessible name is now description, currency and value, status and date, joined with commas (“Paid to Priya Sharma, ₹1,200, Paid, 21 Oct 2026”; TransactionBubble.tsx lines 110–144, 242–250), and with a statusSlot it reads the slot's status, date, text or label instead (133–140, 237–240); the description's weight is read from transactionBubble/description/fontWeight, 500, so it is Medium like Figma (198–202, 226); the static bubble has role text (native) and group with its aria-label (web), and takes testID and rest props (292–322); disableTruncation also lets the status line wrap and drops its fixed 18 px height (267, 274); with status left out, the word comes from the mode's transactionStatus/copy token (207–211). So three guide sentences are stale on the installed build and are left out of the entry: States “Its default name is the description and the status word, with no amount or date, so set accessibilityLabel.”; Sources “its description is Regular where Figma’s is Medium, and its default accessible name leaves out the amount and date”; and Configuration “No other mode changes the bubble.”, which the package's tokens contradict (resolved with its own getVariableByName: Page type JioPlus turns the amount and the chevron white; context 10 jioPlus and context5 Fullscreen Modal or Mode 1 turn the chevron white; Context2 AppBar makes the chevron 32 × 32 and NavArrow Direction Top&Bottom turns it). They are in the human flag (reviews/transactionbubble.json) for a guide fix. The Content sentence “When the bubble presses, set accessibilityLabel to the person, the amount, the status, and the date.” is kept: it still holds (accessibilityLabel replaces the default name), though the default name now carries those four parts when description names the person. Every other sentence used was read against the installed source: no width of its own, it fills its host (213–219, 315); padding 16, radius 23, border 1 rgb(229,229,229), background white, gap 8 and wrap gap 8 (186–192, resolved); description 14/17 on one line unless disableTruncation (195–196, 284); the amount is a MoneyValue from value and currency at Context3 Transaction Bubble, which the bubble forces (180–184, 285; ₹ 28 px on a 34 px line, amount 26, weight 900); the status row is a TransactionStatus from status and date followed by a NavArrow Forward, both with the bubble's modes (260–279); Transaction Status defaults to Expired on the bubble (181), whatever the collection's own default (Request, as the generated mode fact says), so the evidence fact records Expired; the mark is a tick for Paid, a cross for Declined and “!” for Request and Expired, coloured rgb(240,109,15), rgb(37,171,33), rgb(245,0,49) and rgb(181,181,181) (TransactionStatus.tsx 13–21, 103, 116, resolved); children sit between the amount and the status row with the bubble's modes, a child's own modes winning (229–231, 287; react-utils cloneChildrenWithModes); statusSlot replaces the whole row, chevron included, and gets the bubble's modes (233–235, 260); with onPress the root is a Pressable button at opacity 0.85 while pressed (297–310). Height: 16 + 17 + 8 + 34 + 8 + 18 + 16 + 2 px of border = 119 with one line, as the guide says. The Request mode's copy token reads “Expired” (TransactionStatus.tsx 96–98, Marcin's call per the TransactionStatus entry); the guide says to write status, so the bubble's examples always pass the word. Storybook: on 29 October the published Storybook (index.json last modified 17 October 2026) still has the Default, Successful transaction, With press and slot and Dark mode stories; Successful transaction sets no Transaction Status mode beside “Completed”, and With press and slot puts a second MoneyValue in children, so the Sources gap still holds: that build predates dbe0e02, so a bubble with no mode takes the collection default, Request, and its “!” is orange (the evidence's 25 October Discrepancies say the same); this check is recorded here only. Consistency: the TransactionStatus entry's thread example (examples/2) gives each bubble style width 231 with maxWidth 100%, the words in status and date, and the Transaction Status mode on the bubble; this entry says the same (the bubble fills its host, the thread sets 231 px, the mode sets the mark, status and date the words), and its In context example uses the same width, aligning sent bubbles right and received ones left with alignSelf as the guide does. Not recorded: Color Mode and the Dark mode story (the evidence's Limits); Figma's variable names and hex values; the playground; testID, webAccessibilityProps, accessibilityHint and inherited Pressable props; Figma's one Description property and its nested instances (the Sources note's comparison, not usage). Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every bubble), and no Slot gap on the VStack (the guide's M only changes the look; no guide sentence says the content needs it). The Transaction Status mode is set because the guide's Do & Don't says the word alone leaves the grey “!”. Width and alignSelf go through style, as the evidence's Hosting says the guide does; no colour, border, radius or font. Text takes text, as its undocumented entry does. All components used have an entry in this pack (TransactionStatus, Text, VStack). The empty onPress functions stand for opening the payment's details. Left out of examples (three at most): the Paid and Declined cards, the Picture and Button cards, the One line and Wrapped cards, and the Do & Don't pairs. Sorting (batch 11, two cross-check runs). Round 1 flagged /examples/2 (the statusSlot bubble without its own status prop would be named “… • Expired”), from the evidence's 25 October Web render line “With `statusSlot`, the default `aria-label` still says the `status` prop”; on the installed dbe0e02 that no longer holds (with a slot the name reads the slot's status and date, and status no longer defaults to Expired; TransactionBubble.tsx 133–140, 207–211, 237–240), so the example is unchanged and the flag did not recur. Round 1's notes also said /configuration/5 turned the In context sentence on each bubble's onPress into a rule for every bubble, which States contradicts (a bubble with no onPress is a picture): our misreading, reworded to “In a thread, each bubble’s onPress opens that payment’s details.” Round 2, on the final entry, raised no flags; its note asks a person to confirm the Storybook gap, which the 29 October check above does. No dismissals. Left: the human flag for the three stale guide sentences (guide fix). Ticket (coordinator, batch 11): the guide fix belongs to #395 (Component Fix, open), whose publish re-checks the guide; a work note on #395 lists the three sentences, and the human flag points there.

examples.purpose: Payments in a thread, the guide's In context: the payment you sent sits on the right and the request you received on the left, each 231 px wide as in Figma, with the Transaction Status mode that goes with its word and an accessibilityLabel with the person, the amount, the status and the date. Each onPress opens that payment's details; the empty functions stand for that wiring.

    description="Paid to Priya Sharma"
    value="1,200"
    status="Paid"
    date="21 Oct 2026"
    modes={{ 'Transaction Status': 'Paid' }}
    onPress={() => {}}
    accessibilityLabel="Paid to Priya Sharma, ₹1,200, paid 21 Oct 2026"
  />

    style={{ width: 231, maxWidth: '100%', alignSelf: 'flex-start' }}
    description="Request from Priya Sharma"
    value="450"
    status="Requested"
    date="Today"
    modes={{ 'Transaction Status': 'Request' }}
    onPress={() => {}}
    accessibilityLabel="Request from Priya Sharma, ₹450, requested today"
  />
</VStack>

evidenceFacts.name: Transaction Status
evidenceFacts.description: Sets the status mark: Request an orange “!”, Paid a green tick, Declined a red cross, Expired a grey “!”. With no Transaction Status mode the bubble is the Expired mode: a grey “!”.
evidenceFacts.quote: With only Color Mode Light the bubble is the Expired mode: a grey “!” (checked in this run).

evidenceFacts.name: status
evidenceFacts.description: The status line stays on one line: in a 231 px bubble a long status and date end in an ellipsis, and the chevron stays inside.
evidenceFacts.quote: In a 231 px bubble “Declined · 21 October 2026, 4:15 pm” ellipsizes (text 39–204 px) and the chevron stays inside (208–214).

evidenceFacts.name: value
evidenceFacts.description: Shown by a MoneyValue. The amount is announced once, as an image named with the currency and the digits (“₹1,200”); the visible ₹ and digits are hidden from screen readers.
evidenceFacts.quote: the amount is announced once as an image named “₹1,200” (its visible ₹ and digits are hidden)

evidenceFacts.name: currency
evidenceFacts.description: Defaults to ₹; ISO codes such as INR show their symbol. The amount is drawn at the bubble's size: ₹ 28 px, digits 26 px, weight 900.
evidenceFacts.quote: `currency` (default '₹'; ISO codes map) feed a MoneyValue at Context3 Transaction Bubble: ₹ 28 px, amount 26 px, weight 900.

evidenceFacts.name: children
evidenceFacts.description: Rendered between the amount and the status row, with the bubble's modes (a child's own modes win).
evidenceFacts.quote: `children`: rendered between the amount and the status row, with the bubble's modes (child's own modes win).

evidenceFacts.name: statusSlot
evidenceFacts.description: Replaces the whole status row, chevron included; what it holds gets the bubble's modes.
evidenceFacts.quote: `statusSlot`: replaces the whole status row, chevron included, with the bubble's modes.

evidenceFacts.name: onPress
evidenceFacts.description: Makes the root a Pressable button, at opacity 0.85 while pressed.
evidenceFacts.quote: `onPress`: the root becomes a Pressable button (opacity 0.85 while pressed)

evidenceFacts.name: style
evidenceFacts.description: Goes after the container style. The bubble sets no width: it fills its host.
evidenceFacts.quote: `style` goes after the container style. No width: it fills its host.
